title: On Winning the esteem of the whole parish
subtitle: 成功成就 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 成功成就（做人与做事·成功与成就）
meta: 主题语境：成功成就（做人与做事·成功与成就）　|　核心词汇：win　|　正文 357 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 win 的形式与含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1958 the tailor ① winned the esteem of the whole parish with great care, and every customer in the shop said it was the first time anybody had done such a thing there. Three weeks on, people still spoke of how quietly it was done and of how, ever since, the tailor ② wins the esteem of the whole parish on the same day without being asked. My mother said later that to ③ win the esteem of the whole parish at all was the part nobody had expected.

By then somebody had surely ④ winned the esteem of the whole parish before — a line in the order for November 1952 hints at it — but nobody could name the person. ⑤ Winning the esteem of the whole parish with great care, the tailor said once, is nine parts patience and one part nerve; it is not the doing of it that people remember.

My uncle, who kept the needle at the far mirror, meant the other thing entirely. He said that if anybody should ever ⑥ win by twenty clear votes on the same day, nobody should do it twice or speak of it again. The rule the old hands handed down was plainer still: ⑦ Win by twenty clear votes at once and never mention it again.

By 1965 the whole business had shrunk to half a line in the order, and a new customer from the next shop ⑧ wins by twenty clear votes with great care every week without once asking what it had cost the first time. My mother, who had watched all of it from the mirror, said nothing at all; she simply ⑨ winned the esteem of the whole parish again when nobody else would.

⑩ To win the esteem of the whole parish, my mother said in 1970, is not one thing but two: what you do and what the shop remembers of it. She said the second half never grows lighter, and nowadays, whenever the shop forgets, somebody wins the esteem of the whole parish on the same day again and somebody must win the esteem of the whole parish with great care all over again.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请为文中十处画线形式选择对应的用法说明。
options: A. v. 赢得（一般过去式 winned the esteem of the whole parish：1958 年裁缝头一回这样做，小心翼翼地）
B. v. 赢得（一般现在 wins the esteem of the whole parish：自那以后成了老习惯，不必有人开口）
C. v. 赢得（不定式 to win the esteem of the whole parish：文中两处，一是母亲说的“难就难在……”，一是结尾那句格言）
D. v. 赢得（过去完成时 had winned the esteem of the whole parish：1952 年十一月的订单簿上那行字之前就有人做过）
E. v. 赢得（动名词 winning the esteem of the whole parish 作主语：“九分耐心、一分胆气”那一句）
F. v. 获胜（win by twenty clear votes：should ever 之后的原形，指万一真要去获胜以二十票的明显优势获胜）
G. v. 获胜（win by twenty clear votes：祈使句，转述老手们当年立下的那条规矩）
H. v. 赢得（后段两处：新来的顾客照例 wins by twenty clear votes，而母亲又一次 winned the esteem of the whole parish）

answers.why: win 意为“赢得”，1958 年裁缝小心翼翼地赢得赢得整个教区的敬重，那是裁缝铺里头一回有人肯这么做，故用一般过去式 winned。
win 意为“赢得”，自那以后裁缝当天就把这件事做了一遍又一遍，不必有人开口，故用一般现在 wins。
win 意为“赢得”，母亲说的是“难就难在肯赢得赢得整个教区的敬重”，此处为不定式 to win the esteem of the whole parish。
win 意为“赢得”，订单簿里 十一月 那行字说明早在 1965 年之前就有人赢得过，故用过去完成时 had winned。
win 意为“赢得”，裁缝说“赢得赢得整个教区的敬重这件事是九分耐心一分胆气”，此处 winning the esteem of the whole parish 作主语。
win 意为“获胜”，叔叔说的是“万一真有人去获胜以二十票的明显优势获胜”，should ever 之后用原形 win by twenty clear votes。
win 意为“获胜”，老手们留下的规矩是祈使句：立刻获胜以二十票的明显优势获胜（win by twenty clear votes at once），以后再也不要提起。
win 意为“赢得”，新来的顾客每个星期都照例获胜以二十票的明显优势获胜，从不问头一回的代价，用一般现在 wins。
win 意为“赢得”，母亲在无人肯做的时候又一次小心翼翼地赢得赢得整个教区的敬重，用一般过去式 winned 叙述。
win 意为“赢得”，结尾那句是母亲 1970 年的话：要赢得赢得整个教区的敬重，其实不是一件事，而是两件事——你做的那一件，和裁缝铺记住的那一件。

task3.title: Task 3　语境写作
task3.intro: 请写 5—6 个句子，至少使用 win 的 3 种不同形式（过去式、第三人称、-ing、不定式等）；至少使用下列词语中的 3 个。
answers: In 1958 the tailor winned the esteem of the whole parish with great care, and nobody in the shop forgot it.
Even now the tailor wins the esteem of the whole parish on the same day whenever the shop asks.
Winning the esteem of the whole parish with great care, my mother used to say, is nine parts patience and one part nerve.
If anybody should ever win by twenty clear votes on the same day, nobody should do it twice or speak of it again.
A new customer from the next shop wins by twenty clear votes with great care every week, asking nothing about the past.
When nobody else would, my mother winned the esteem of the whole parish again, and the shop remembered that half.
